entry_fields.id: stable slug identifying the entry; existing claim bindings connect Part V's hand-written figures and named cases to these ids
entry_fields.claim: one sentence, stated the way the book would state it
entry_fields.value: number, [low, high] range, or structured object
entry_fields.source: title / venue / year / locator (doi or url); for papers, the PINNED version
entry_fields.retrieved: ISO date the value was last checked against the source; year-month permitted for entries ported from book.md's reference section, whose figures were last verified July 2026
entry_fields.method: how the value was obtained: quoted, derived, fetched-by-script
entry_fields.fetch: script under registry/fetch/ that can refresh this value, or null for pinned papers
entry_fields.notes: caveats that must travel with the number
entry_fields.book: which book's claims need this entry: book-1 (Part V/method evidence), book-2 (transition/tech/costing), legacy-only (candidate for the deletion manifest's consciously-dropped list); absent = book-1

claims.claim: During Jharkhand's biometric-authentication reforms, 1.5–2 million legitimate beneficiaries lost access to benefits at some point.
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar, "Identity Verification Standards in Welfare Programs: Experimental Evidence from India", Review of Economics and Statistics 107(2): 372-392 (2025), doi:10.1162/rest_a_01296, https://doi.org/10.1162/rest_a_01296; published abstract distributed by MIT Press through RePEc, https://ideas.repec.org/a/tpr/restat/v107y2025i2p372-392.html
claims.method: published abstract checked through the publisher-supplied RePEc record
claims.notes: The published abstract gives 1.5–2 million legitimate beneficiaries losing access at some point and attributes much of the adverse effect to transition protocols. The final full article was unavailable; the UCSD author manuscript failed TLS verification, including outside the sandbox, and NBER access returned 403. No fresh inspection of the final study’s tables or replication is claimed. The abstract’s range is retained as an attributed estimate, not a ration-card count.

claims.claim: In the reconciliation phase, roughly 1.7 million people did not receive PDS benefits in the first month (July 2017).
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar (2025), REStat 107(2), body
claims.notes: ~1.2 million under the paper's conservative assumption. The widely quoted '13%' is a percentage-POINT increase in non-receipt in treated blocks, not a share of all beneficiaries.

claims.claim: 88% of cancelled ration cards sampled in the study districts belonged to genuine households.
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar (2025), REStat 107(2)
claims.method: quoted; authors label the figure 'purely descriptive' (non-causal)
claims.notes: Covers the 1.44 lakh cancellations in the 10 study districts — never to be narrated as the Drèze survey's 11 lakh statewide figure.

claims.claim: Drèze and coauthors report mass cancellation of Jharkhand ration cards not linked to Aadhaar after the chief secretary’s order of 27 March 2017, including exclusion of eligible people.
claims.source: Drèze, Khalid, Khera & Somanchi, "Aadhaar and Food Security in Jharkhand: Pain without Gain?", Economic and Political Weekly 52(50): 50-60 (16 December 2017), https://www.epw.in/journal/2017/50/special-articles/aadhaar-and-food-security-jharkhand.html; p. 58, Postscript; coauthor-hosted copy https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Nazar-Khalid-3/publication/322151401_Aadhaar_and_food_security_in_Jharkhand_Pain_without_gain/links/5be662a74585150b2bab8a2f/Aadhaar-and-food-security-in-Jharkhand-Pain-without-gain.pdf
claims.notes: The EPW site returned 403; the coauthor-hosted article was inspected through the browser. Its Postscript supports mass cancellation but the previous 1.1-million-card figure was not located and is withdrawn from this entry and Part V. The 11.2-lakh figure on p. 52 is a conditional extrapolation of transaction failures, not the cancellation count. The study’s household sample is not a statewide card census.

claims.claim: Lin proposes that removal of collective members’ right to withdraw in 1958 undermined a self-enforcing agreement and contributed to the agricultural productivity collapse; the paper presents evidence consistent with that hypothesis.

The other works in the source field remain background, not newly inspected evidence.

claims.claim: Abramitzky examines equal sharing, selection, exit and incentive pressures in the kibbutzim. Leviatan reports that roughly three-quarters had adopted differential salaries by 2011; neither figure isolates leadership rotation as the cause of reform.
claims.source: For community count and incentive analysis: Abramitzky, "Lessons from the Kibbutz on the Equality-Incentives Trade-Off", Journal of Economic Perspectives 25(1): 185-208 (2011), doi:10.1257/jep.25.1.185, https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/jep.25.1.185; Abramitzky, The Mystery of the Kibbutz, Princeton UP (2018). For the differential-salary series: Uriel Leviatan, Lessons from the Kibbutz as a Real Utopia, p. 12, https://www.sscc.wisc.edu/soc/faculty/pages/wright/ASA/Leviatan%20--%20lessons%20from%20the%20kibbutz%20as%20real%20utopia.pdf; JEP author copy, community count p. 186, https://ranabr.people.stanford.edu/sites/g/files/sbiybj26066/files/media/file/abramitzky_jep.pdf
claims.notes: Checked the JEP article’s 268-community count and its discussion of incentives, selection and exit, and Leviatan p. 12 (21% in 1999; 76% in 2011). The 2018 monograph was not newly read. These are historical populations, not a current census; the review neither reconstructs the counts nor isolates leadership rotation as their cause.

claims.claim: Scott reports at least five million people relocated during the 1973–1976 Tanzanian campaign. He quotes Nyerere’s higher claim for village residents; it is a different population, not an agreed count of forced moves.
claims.units: people relocated; reported village residents (distinct populations)
claims.source: Scott, Seeing Like a State, Yale UP (1998), ch. 7, https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctt1nq3vk; chapter opening and “Bureaucratic Convenience, Bureaucratic Interests”; inspected transcription https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/james-c-scott-seeing-like-a-state

The opening’s note questions an official nine-million relocation claim; the later speech quotes 13,065,000 village residents. Neither number is an independent census. The reader keeps the populations distinct and draws no causal conclusion from their disagreement.

claims.claim: In Auroville Foundation v. Natasha Storey (2025), the Supreme Court upheld the Board’s authority to constitute its development council without reserved Assembly places, distinguishing consultation on formulating the master plan from its implementation.

claims.notes: Read the original judgment, including the quoted statutes and paragraphs 12–17. The Assembly’s statutory consultation role in formulating the master plan is not erased. The case concerns Board authority over implementation committees, not a finding that all state intervention is justified. It is distinct from the same day’s environmental-jurisdiction case.

claims.notes: Checked poem 32, subtitle Varam Kettal, fourth stanza and surrounding address to Shakti against Project Madurai’s Tamil transcription. Unicode composition and caesura placement differ without changing the words. The book’s own English rendering retains its delegated approval recorded under item 13. claims.claim: In the bundled 141-country snapshot, the correlation between electoral democracy and mean life evaluation is about 0.51 before, and about 0.20 after, adjusting for log GDP per capita. This is descriptive association, not a causal allocation between income and democracy.
claims.source: Derived by registry/fetch/vdem_happiness.py from OWID grapher series (CC BY): electoral-democracy-index (V-Dem v2x_polyarchy) https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/electoral-democracy-index, happiness-cantril-ladder (WHR) https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/happiness-cantril-ladder, gdp-per-capita-worldbank https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-worldbank; latest observation per series, each year ≥ 2022 (years can differ within a country); snapshot registry/data/vdem-happiness-2026-08-03.csv
claims.notes: Snapshot reproduced 2026-09-21 without refetching or advancing its retrieval date. Countries are equally weighted; three GDP observations are from 2024 while the other year labels are 2025. Adjustment can remove confounding or part of a causal pathway; this analysis does not identify which. It establishes neither material provision as the cause of most wellbeing differences nor an ordering of political and material rights. See book-1/source/vdem-rederivation.md. OWID’s source definitions were checked: the 2025 ladder label averages 2023–2025 surveys (0–10); GDP is PPP per capita in constant 2021 international dollars.

claims.claim: In the bundled cross-section, adjacent Regimes of the World category means differ by +0.02, +0.59 and +1.09 Cantril-ladder points. These compare different groups of countries and do not estimate gains from regime transitions.
claims.source: Same derivation as vdem-2026-democracy-happiness-partial, adding the OWID political-regime series for the Regimes of the World categories https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/political-regime
claims.notes: Snapshot reproduced 2026-09-21 without refetching or advancing its retrieval date. Category means are unadjusted for income and other country differences. Steps use unrounded means. The small lowest-category difference is not evidence that partial democratisation has no benefit. A cross-section does not supply a transition counterfactual.

claims.claim: The exploratory absolute-residual regression on the bundled V-Dem snapshot has a negative democracy coefficient after income adjustment, using conventional standard errors. It measures neither a guaranteed wellbeing floor nor the lower tail of individual lives.
claims.source: Same derivation as vdem-2026-democracy-happiness-partial (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/electoral-democracy-index and siblings); the isolation test against the alternative index is recorded qualitatively in book-1/source/vdem-rederivation.md, its coefficients deliberately kept out of this CC0 registry under the 2026-08-02 licensing ruling
claims.notes: Snapshot reproduced 2026-09-21 without refetching or advancing its retrieval date. Absolute residuals from ladder~polyarchy are fitted on polyarchy and log GDP; they include both tails of country means. Standard errors are conventional, not heteroskedasticity-robust. The EIU comparison in the working record was not reproduced and its inputs are not bundled; Part V no longer uses it as empirical support. The historical record and licensing restriction remain. A significance-label contrast would not itself test a difference between coefficients.

claims.claim: The prior democracy/happiness analysis behind Part V's worked example, independently re-derived on openly licensed instruments (source reference only).
claims.source: demo-happy.txt (repository root), computed over democracy_vs_happiness_144.csv: WHR 2025 life evaluations (2022–2024 average) merged with EIU Democracy Index 2025, 144 countries matched from EIU's 166 and WHR's 147
claims.notes: PRIOR ANALYSIS, RECORDED FOR PROVENANCE, NOT AS EVIDENCE. Every figure Part V uses comes from the V-Dem re-derivation (vdem-2026-*), and no EIU-derived value enters this CC0 registry, per the 2026-08-02 licensing ruling. The re-derivation reproduced the income narrowing and the step pattern and did NOT reproduce this analysis's headline dispersion finding — see vdem-2026-floor-claim-instrument-fragile. The merged CSV sits in the repository root under the root LICENSE, committed before that ruling, and carries EIU index values; whether the repository may grant CC0 over a non-redistributable index is an open question for the author, recorded in CLAUDE.md under the pending obligations that outlived the retired root tracker.

claims.claim: Santoshi Kumari, eleven, died on 28 September 2017 in Simdega district, Jharkhand, months after her family's ration card was cancelled for want of an Aadhaar link; her family said she died asking for rice, and the district administration said the cause was malaria rather than starvation.
claims.source: Aarefa Johari, Scroll.in, 16 October 2017, opening account and “Died asking for rice”, https://scroll.in/article/854225/denied-food-because-she-did-not-have-aadhaar-linked-ration-card-jharkhand-girl-dies-of-starvation; Jaideep Deogharia, The Times of India, 17 October 2017, opening paragraphs quoting deputy commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri, https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ranchi/11-year-old-dies-activists-cry-hunger-jharkhand-government-says-malaria/articleshow/61110050.cms
claims.notes: Checked the family and activist account, reported confirmation of cancellation, and the deputy commissioner’s contrary malaria explanation. Neither account is adjudicated here. Scroll’s 28 September 2018 follow-up does not repeat the malaria dispute and no longer supplies that citation. These are reports of testimony and official statements, not medical records or an independent cause-of-death finding.

claims.claim: EPI’s projected 2025 estimate puts realized CEO compensation at the largest 350 US firms by sales at about 325 times typical-worker compensation.
claims.units: mean of firm-specific CEO-to-industry-worker compensation ratios
claims.source: Bivens, Gould and Kandra, CEO Pay, Economic Policy Institute (15 September 2026), Figure A, Table 1 and their methods notes, https://www.epi.org/publication/ceo-pay/
claims.notes: Checked Figure A, Table 1 and notes. The 324.7 ratio is projected from partial reporting. Worker compensation is average wages and benefits for full-time, full-year production and nonsupervisory workers in each firm’s industry. It is neither the firm’s median nor its lowest salary. Realized CEO compensation includes exercised options and vested awards. Unlike MONDRAGON’s salary scale, this cannot identify a governance effect.

claims.claim: Adjustment for a regression covariate can alter the causal quantity of interest; whether a control helps depends on the causal structure.
claims.source: Cinelli, Carlos, Andrew Forney and Judea Pearl. A Crash Course in Good and Bad Controls. Sociological Methods & Research 53(3), 1071–1104 (2024; online 2022). https://doi.org/10.1177/00491241221099552; author-hosted reprint https://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/r493-reprint.pdf
claims.notes: Checked the publisher’s full text, Models 11–12 and total versus direct effects. This is methodological guidance, not an empirical study of the proposed constitution.

claims.claim: A contrast between a statistically significant estimate and a nonsignificant estimate does not itself establish a statistically significant difference between them.
claims.source: Gelman, Andrew and Hal Stern. The Difference Between Significant and Not Significant Is Not Itself Statistically Significant. The American Statistician 60(4), 328–331 (2006). https://doi.org/10.1198/000313006X152649; author-hosted copy https://sites.stat.columbia.edu/gelman/surveys.course/GelmanStern2006.pdf
claims.notes: Checked the author-hosted article, pp. 328–329. This is methodological guidance, not an empirical study of the proposed constitution.

claims.claim: Scientific conclusions should not turn only on whether a p-value crosses a threshold; statistical significance does not measure effect size or practical importance.
claims.source: American Statistical Association, Statement on Statistical Significance and P-Values (2016). https://www.amstat.org/asa/files/pdfs/p-valuestatement.pdf; full statement https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2016.1154108
claims.notes: Checked the ASA release dated 7 March 2016, p. 2, principles 3 and 5. This is methodological guidance, not an empirical study of the proposed constitution.

claims.claim: Article 67 of Germany's Basic Law requires the Bundestag to elect a successor when withdrawing confidence from the Chancellor; constructive replacement is compatible with a prime-ministerial executive.

claims.notes: The current German statutory text was read on the retrieval date. This establishes a constitutional provision, not its causal effects or the superiority of either executive design.
